verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (29 October 2025): a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would amend penal-code article 225 to punish conduct 'contrary to biological sex' with up to 3 years in prison and would allow charges for anyone taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony (up to 4 years) plus, under civil-code article 40, raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate (providers facing fines and up to 7 years, patients up to 3 years); 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected and HRW calls for withdrawal. This is the national framework this province's record stands under; the article records no province-specific enforcement or incidents.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Kaos GL's LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 ('A Major Siege', published 24 February 2026) finds hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 under 'Year of the Family' instructions, documenting six right-to-life violations including three hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (up from 51), and 313 right-to-liberty violations (about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions); the state keeps no official hate-crime statistics, so data rely on media coverage. It is a national-level report and contains no province-specific detail.
